newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German 97 M3 target at 3.5-6.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German 97 M3 target at 3.5-6.5 pct.

text.p: The following are the views expressed by economists after the Bundesbank set its M3 money supply growth corridor for 1997 at 3.5 to 6.5 percent, compared to the four to seven percent target range for 1996 and said it was extending its orientation to a two year period.
A Reuter poll of economists predicted that the growth corridor would be unchanged or slightly lower than in 1996 and some economists had expected the two-year target.
GERTRUDE TRAUD, ECONOMIST, BANK JULIUS BAER, FRANKFURT:
"The 3.5 to 6.5 percent M3 corridor is as expected. The Bundesbank has stayed faithful to their aims."

"The new M3 goal will have no influence on the market and is no surprise. The longer-term money supply goal of two years should ease problems in the run up to monetary union. The lower corridor indicated that the inflation goal is also half a percent lower. It should also play a role that the long-term production potential has sunk somewhat."

FRANK SCHROEDER, ANALYST, TRINKAUS CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, FRANKFURT: "The new corridor is as we expected. Interesting is the two year orientation, because it means a target for 1998 when monetary union participants will be decided.
STEFAN SCHNEIDER, PARIBAS CAPITAL MARKETS, FRANKFURT:

" A two year goal has been set now because the Bundesbank would have come under political pressure if it had set the target at the end of 1997. Fundamental factors mean the corridor could have been set a full point lower. But a full point lower would have been seen by the markets as too restrictive."
